Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — we left with a much clearer sense of Redwood's model routing and the caching options. Per our internal kickoff, I've attached a draft MAP and a separate spreadsheet with our baseline traffic profile and cost assumptions. Can you and your team do a quick sanity pass on the tokens/$ numbers and the caching/batching assumptions?

High level asks:
- Confirm realistic tokens-per-call for our clinical summarization flow (we've estimated 350–500 tokens per call).
- Validate the caching hit-rate assumptions for repeated prefixes (we currently model 25% hit rate).
- Is a batching factor of 3–5 reasonable for our 200 rps peak? What ops tradeoffs should we expect?

We're trying to lock the MAP this week so procurement can tie pricing to a pilot start.

Attachments: helixmed_map_draft.xlsx (MAP draft, stages/timeline), token_model_assumptions.pdf (traffic + assumptions)

Thanks — Emma

Hi Emma — thanks for the attachments and the clear asks.

Quick response while we do a short internal pass:
- We'll validate the 350–500 tokens range against the baseline prompt+response for clinical summarization and return a recommended 95th percentile.
- 25% caching hit is plausible depending on how much of the prompt can be canonicalized; we'll run a sample probability estimate and give a conservative/optimistic pair.
- Batching 3–5 sounds reasonable for throughput savings, but the effective batching window depends on your latency SLOs. For 200 rps peak, a mean batch size of ~3 should be feasible without pushing tail latency if we configure continuous batching and a 30–40ms scheduling window.

I'm looping in Neha (cost/econ) and Ben (solutions/ops) to run the numbers and produce a short worksheet we can attach to the MAP. We'll aim to get a marked-up MAP and a simple sensitivity table back to you by Fri EOD PT.

Next step: can you confirm the pilot start target (you mentioned "early Dec") and whether procurement needs a fixed unit price or tiered usage bands for the pilot?

Cheers,
Chloe

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP — cost assumptions for evaluation phase (draft attached)

Chloe / team — putting together the quick financial sanity worksheet. Draft notes below; I'll attach the sheet after we confirm a couple of inputs.

Summary (initial pass):
- Baseline token cost we should model (hosted): $0.0007 per token (this maps to our current public hosted blended rate for medium-context models).
- Recommended modeling values: avg tokens/call = 420 (we'll provide 10th/50th/90th percentiles after sample run).
- Caching: assume a conservative KV prefix hit of 20% and an optimistic hit of 32%. For HelixMed's clinical templates, optimistic seems reachable if they canonicalize templates during integration. A hit reduces compute token bill only when prefix tokens are reused locally (we model an effective cost reduction proportional to hit rate).
- Batching: for continuous batching on our runtime, mean batch size of 3 reduces per-token GPU time ~10–14% in typical seq-length mixes; batch of 5 can get ~18–22% savings but increases tail latency risk under spiky traffic.
- Quantization/instance mix: recommend modeling a q8_0-equivalent performance profile for Dedicated pilot (40% lower GPU cost vs fp16 in our internal benchmarks). If HelixMed must use Hosted, reduce that benefit to 25% due to multi-tenant overhead.

Sensitivity table (quick):
- tokens/call +/-20% -> cost per 1,000 calls changes roughly +/-20% (linear).
- cache hit +/-10ppt -> effective per-call compute cost swing of ~ -8% to +8% depending on tokens saved.
- batching variability (mean 3 vs mean 5) -> unit cost swing of ~6–9% between configurations when everything else is fixed.

Open items I need from HelixMed to finalize worksheet:
1) sample size for call payloads (we asked for 200 anonymized example requests in the MAP; is that possible?)
2) strict latency SLO for the pilot (95th percentile target) — this drives our batching window recommendation.
3) confirm whether prefix canonicalization is part of integration (that increases cache hit dramatically).

I'll attach helixmed_map_financial_sanity.xlsx after Ben confirms the batching assumptions and we run a quick micro-sim.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Product Economist, Redwood Inference

Chloe / Neha — this is extremely helpful, thank you.

A few quick answers to your open items:

2) Pilot latency SLO: 95th <= 500ms (our clinicians prefer sub-1s interactive responses).
3) Yes — prefix canonicalization is part of the integration workstream; we expect templating to cover ~60% of repeatable text for the summaries.

Pilot start: HelixMed is still aiming for the week of Dec 6 for a 2-week evaluation window. Procurement would prefer a fixed blended unit price for the pilot (so they can approve purchase orders) — can Redwood propose a pilot unit price that maps to the modeled tokens/$ plus an agreed rollout discount if we move to Dedicated?

Thanks again — Emma
